subject: Request for CEO approval: tiered liability schedule + custom indemnity carveout
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah@novumtech.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Amir Shah <contracts@novumtech.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: NovumTech SOW redlines — liability & indemnity asks

Jonas / Aditya —

Thanks for the demo last week. We reviewed the draft SOW and have three items that will need to be cleared before legal will sign:

1) Liability cap: NovumTech requires a graduated liability schedule tied to run-rate rather than a flat $1M cap. Proposal: 6 months run-rate = $250k cap, 12 months = $750k cap, >12 months = 2x ARR up to $2M.

2) Indemnity carveout: we need an express carveout for third-party IP claims related to NovumTech’s integrations and custom connectors.

3) Warranty language: extend warranty remedies from 30 to 90 days for any performance regressions that affect throughput SLAs.

We can offset these by taking a 15% concession on list pricing in year 1. Please let me know who we need to get sign-off from on your side — our procurement would like to circulate a fully executed SOW by 9/15.

Attached: NovumTech_SOW_v3_redlines.pdf (redline), liability_tradeoffs.docx (internal analysis)

Regards,
Sarah Lin
Head of Procurement, NovumTech

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah@novumtech.com>, Amir Shah <contracts@novumtech.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: NovumTech SOW redlines — liability & indemnity asks

Marissa —

Forwarding Novum’s redlines. High level: they want a graduated cap, an indemnity carveout for their integrations, and a longer warranty window. They propose a 15% year-1 concession as the commercial trade-off.

Why I’m escalating: the graduated cap and carveout are non-standard. I ran quick numbers — the proposed escalator to 2x ARR up to $2M materially increases tail risk on a multi-year relationship. However, Novum is strategic (large, product integrations + potential ISV partnership). We have three levers:

- Approve as-is (exec sign-off) and accept 15% discount;
- Offer middle ground: capped escalator but with a qualifying SLA threshold (e.g., applies only for sustained breaches >3 months), and limit carveout to documented third-party connectors validated by Redwood;
- Reject and push for the standard $1M cap + limited indemnity for direct Redwood IP only.

Proposed recommended path: ask for CEO sign-off to approve a conditioned graduated cap (2-tier: $500k at 12 months, $1.5M at >24 months) tied to uptime/throughput commitments and revert indemnity carveout into a scoped schedule (only integrations built by Novum or third-party connectors that Novum introduced). Legal input needed on precise wording.

Can you review and give redline suggestions? Aditya, if we move forward cost-side, confirm you can absorb the 15% discount under the deal economics or propose an alternative commercial offset (credits, term extension, seats).

Goal: please get legal language back to me by EOD tomorrow so I can present to the CEO on Friday morning.

Thanks,
Jonas
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>, Sarah Lin <sarah@novumtech.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: NovumTech SOW redlines — liability & indemnity asks

Jonas —

Thanks for the context. Quick thoughts (high level legal guidance):

1) Graduated liability schedule: we can accept a tiered approach but must tie increases to objective metrics and successful adoption milestones (e.g., production run-rate verified by telemetry + acceptance tests at 12 and 24 months). Without objective triggers the escalator is indefensible. Suggested clause: liability cap increases only upon mutually agreed adoption milestones and on condition that customer has not materially modified the connectors without Redwood’s documented guidance.

2) Indemnity carveout: we cannot broadly carve out indemnity for third-party IP claims. We can carve out liability for customer-introduced third-party connectors provided Novum: (a) warrants they own or have license to the connectors, and (b) provides indemnities to Redwood for those connectors. Alternatively, we accept a narrow contractual representation about customer-supplied integrations and limit Redwood’s exposure to failures in our delivered code.

3) Warranty window: extending remedies to 90 days is acceptable for performance regressions that Redwood caused. We should keep remedy types limited (patch, rollback, credits) and preserve exclusion for performance issues caused by customer environments or third-party integrations.

Redline recommendations attached: NovumTech_SOW_v3_redlines_MCOLE.pdf. Also attaching recommended fallback language that can be presented to execs as a risk-mitigated option.

Risk note for execs: accepting the proposed escalator without telemetry/adoption gates may set a precedent for other large deals. If execs are comfortable, I recommend requiring: (i) legal representation & indemnity from Novum on customer-supplied connectors, (ii) clear adoption milestones, and (iii) a hard overall cap (e.g., not exceeding $2M).

If this aligns with commercial, I can format a 1-page summary for CEO sign-off.

Marissa Cole
VP, Legal — Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah@novumtech.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 17:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: NovumTech SOW redlines — liability & indemnity asks

Quick note — I support the conditioned graduated cap approach Marissa outlined. Commercially, we can accept a 12-month effective discount of 12% (vs Novum’s 15%) if the following are agreed:

- Adoption milestones at 6 and 12 months with objective telemetry;
- Novum provides a warranty & indemnity for any customer-supplied connectors and lists them in an annex;
- Remedies for warranty breaches limited to patching, rollback, and service credits (no unlimited support obligations).

If legal can draft the CEO one-pager with those guardrails, I will commit to the revised commercial and escalate pricing approval internally.

Aditya Rao
VP Sales, North America
Redwood Inference
